SMTO-EXE-0031 — SMTO gave one input two different values

GUID: 423475b1-6d9b-4785-bc64-7ec342d38179
Slug: input-binding-conflict
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO planned a step that fills the same input from two different earlier results, so it couldn't tell which one to use. The step did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment and watch the task. SMTO normally plans the step again with one value for each input. This mix-up is reported back to SMTO so it can correct its own plan.
  2. If the task stops, tell SMTO in the conversation which earlier result to use for that step, for example "use the file list from the first step". Naming one result removes the choice SMTO couldn't make.
  3. Ask SMTO to continue the task. The step never ran, so it is safe to try once the input is clear.

What success looks like

  • The step runs and its output uses the result you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same request unchanged; it will hit the same mix-up.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Input-binding resolution found the same input_name bound more than once in one request and refused to choose between the assignments.

What this means

  • Binding resolution encountered the same destination input_name more than once in a single request and refused to choose between those assignments. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Binding resolution encountered the same destination input_name more than once in a single request and refused to choose between those assignments.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect duplicate input names and their source operation/pointer pairs; choose one exact authoritative source per destination.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the input_bindings of the rejected call (agent_runtime.execution.bindings.resolve_bindings) and keep exactly one binding per input_name, pointing at the intended source_operation_id and source_pointer. Remove the duplicate assignment before the call is resubmitted.
  • Use one exact retained source for each input name and remove conflicting duplicate assignments.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each input name is bound once to the intended retained result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
